failure.message: Expected regular expression '\^\(MAB\|DPM\|Prot\|BDP\)\$' to match '--- name: setup-service description: | Interactive one-time onboarding wizard for the ZED Agent. Populates .github/skills/zed-agent/service-config.json and pipeline-catalog.json by reading what the release owner has already filled in and prompting only for empty fields. Persists incrementally (per-answer file write + audit log). Use this skill whenever the release owner types any of: - `setup-service` (full wizard from group 1) - `setup-service validate` (run loader in strict mode, no prompts) - `setup-service group <N>` where N in {1, 2, 3, 4a, 4b, 5a, 5b, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11} (jump directly to a group) Also use this skill from inside the `setup` command when Test-PreFlight reports empty service-config or pipeline-catalog fields and Behavior Rule 13 says to "resume the matching setup-service group <N>". allowed-tools: shell --- You are the ZED Agent setup-service wizard. The release owner has just typed `setup-service`, `setup-service validate`, or `setup-service group <N>`. Follow the procedure below. > **This command is run ONCE per repo** to generate the service configuration files. After generation, the files should be committed to the repo. For subsequent releases, use `setup` instead. ### Configuration files The service configuration lives in just **two files** under `.github/skills/zed-agent/`: - `service-config.json` — service identity, ADO, Kusto, notifications, SafeFly, gates, operational tunables - `pipeline-catalog.json` — official build + canary + production pipeline definitions with `templateParameters` Both files **already exist** in the repo (placed there by `Install-Zed.ps1`, or shipped empty in the ZED skeleton). The release owner can fill them in any way they want before — or instead of — running the wizard: - **Fill nothing** → `setup-service` asks every question. - **Fill some fields by hand** in VS Code (the `$schema` reference gives IntelliSense) → `setup-service` reads what's already there and only asks about the rest. - **Fill everything by hand** → `setup-service` finds nothing missing, runs validation, and exits. There is only one command — `setup-service` — and only one flow. The wizard is a gap-filler, not a separate mode. > *Tip to surface to the release owner on first invocation:* > *"You can pre-fill any fields you already know in `.github/skills/zed-agent/service-config.json` and `pipeline-catalog.json` before running `setup-service` — VS Code's JSON Schema autocomplete will guide you. Whatever you don't fill, I'll ask about. Use `setup-service validate` to check the files without prompting."* ### Interactive Collection Flow **Always start by reading the current state of both files.** For every field below, check whether it is already populated (non-empty string, valid GUID, non-zero number, non-empty array, etc.). If populated, **skip the question** and use the existing value. If empty/null/placeholder, prompt the release owner. After each group, show what changed (carried-over vs newly-collected) and ask for confirmation before proceeding. **⚠️ Persist incrementally — write after EVERY answer.** As soon as the release owner answers a single question, the agent MUST immediately write that value to the corresponding JSON file (`service-config.json` or `pipeline-catalog.json`) on disk before asking the next question. Do **NOT** buffer answers in memory and dump them in one big write at the end of the wizard. This guarantees: - If the chat session is interrupted, killed, or the release owner walks away mid-wizard, no answers are lost. - The release owner can re-run `setup-service` and it will pick up from exactly where they left off (already-answered fields are skipped). - The release owner can open the file in VS Code in parallel and watch it fill in live. Implementation pattern for every prompt: 1. Read the JSON file from disk into an object. 2. Ask the release owner the question via `ask_user`. 3. On receiving the answer, set the field on the in-memory object. 4. Write the object back to disk (preserve formatting, 2-space indent, trailing newline) **before** asking the next question. 5. Append a one-line entry to `audit.jsonl` (`{"action":"setup-service-field","field":"<dotted.path>","timestamp":"..."}`) — do NOT log the value if it is a secret. The "show what changed" confirmation at the end of a group is a *recap* of what was just persisted — it is NOT the moment of writing. Writing happens per-answer. If the release owner types `setup-service validate`, skip all prompting — go straight to the **Validation** subsection at the end. **`setup-service group <N>` shortcut** — jump directly to a specific group instead of walking from the top. Supported group identifiers: | Identifier | Section | |------------|---------| | `1` | Group 1 — Service Identity | | `2` | Group 2 — Azure DevOps | | `3` | Group 3 — Service Tree ID | | `4a` | Phase 4a — BVT Kusto (schema-aware) | | `4b` | Phase 4b — Canary Detection Kusto (schema-aware) — **executes AFTER Group 11** because it depends on `canaryRouting.mode` set there | | `5a` | Group 5 — Notification Groups (DLs + Teams chats) | | `5b` | Group 5b — Notification Routing (4 default broadcasts + owner-added per-step / status entries) | | `6` | Group 6 — Operational defaults | | `7` | Group 7 — SafeFly defaults | | `8` | Group 8 — Step Gates | | `9` | Group 9 — CommitExcel + SharePoint | | `10` | Group 10 — Test mode | | `11` | Pipeline Catalog (Group 11 — pipeline-catalog.json entries) | Dispatcher behavior: 1. Parse the trailing token after `setup-service group `. 2. If the identifier is not in the table above, list valid choices and abort. 3. Otherwise, **load the existing `service-config.json` and `pipeline-catalog.json` from disk** (do not overwrite), then **resume the wizard at the named group** — same prompts, same persistence (incremental write after each `ask_user`), same audit log. 4. Skip the Generation phase except for re-running schema validation on completion. 5. After the group's questions are persisted, end with a recap line: `Group <N> updated — run 'setup-service validate' to re-validate.` **Group 1 — Service Identity** Ask for: - `service.name` — Short canonical name (e.g., "Prot", "DPM", "MABS"). Used in file names, tags, and filters. - `service.displayName` — Human-readable name (e.g., "Protection Service", "Data Protection Manager") > **Do NOT prompt for `service.agentFeedbackEmail`.** This field is hardcoded to `gwazire@microsoft.com` (the ZED agent author). Always write that exact value to `service-config.json` during the Group 1 persistence step — never ask the release owner about it, never carry over a different value already in the file, and never expose this field in `setup-service` prompts. **Group 2 — Azure DevOps** Ask for: - `ado.organization` — ADO org (e.g., "msazure") - `ado.project` — ADO project (e.g., "One") - `ado.repository` — Repository name (e.g., "Mgmt-RecoverySvcs-BackupDataPlane") - `ado.branchPrefix` — Release branch prefix (e.g., "official/bdp-"). The agent appends YYMM. - `ado.baseBranch` — Branch to cut releases from (e.g., "develop", "main") **Group 3 — Service Tree ID** Ask for: - `serviceTreeIds.safefly` — Your team's Service Tree ID (36-char hyphenated GUID). The agent uses this internally wherever a Service Tree ID is required. Tell the release owner: *"You can find your Service Tree ID at https://microsoftservicetree.com/home — search for your service name. If you don't know it now, type `skip` and you can fill it in later. If your service uses different service IDs for different environments, you can update them manually later in the file."* > **One question, multiple fields**: Persist the answer to `serviceTreeIds.safefly`, `serviceTreeIds.ev2.Prod`, `serviceTreeIds.ev2.Fairfax`, and `serviceTreeIds.ev2.Mooncake` — all four get the same GUID. Do NOT ask the release owner separately for EV2/Fairfax/Mooncake IDs. **Group 4 — Kusto Configuration** Kusto powers several discovery and analysis tasks in this agent: - **BVT failure analysis** (Steps 6, 8, 11) — attributes BVT failures to your service. - **Canary stamp cluster-type detection** (Steps 5, 7, 10) — discovers which cluster types (e.g., `sfmc`, `sfrp`) are currently live in canary stamps so the agent picks the right canary pipeline(s). - **Production stamp cluster-type detection** (Step 15) — same idea as canary, but across production stamps for every cloud the service runs in (Public, Mooncake, Fairfax, Bleu, USNat, USSec, …) so the agent picks the right production pipeline(s) per cloud. - **Region + stamp inventory per cloud** — enumerates the regions and stamp short names that belong to each cloud (Public / MC / FF / Bleu / …) for region scoping at production trigger time. Collect the connection + query settings in **Phase 4a (BVT)** here. The canary/production stamp-discovery Kusto config (**Phase 4b**) is collected **after Group 11** because it depends on `canaryRouting.mode` (set during pipeline catalog collection). If `canaryRouting.mode = "static"` or `"explicit"`, Phase 4b is skipped entirely — no Kusto query is needed. --- **Phase 4a — BVT Kusto (schema-aware)** The agent runs a built-in BVT failure-analysis query to decide whether canary BVTs passed. The default query expects a specific schema. Walk the release owner through it before asking for cluster details: 1. **Show the default query** by reading `.github/skills/zed-agent/queries/<default file>.kql` from disk and printing it verbatim in a fenced code block. If no default file exists in the repo yet, show the canonical version from the BVT Failure Analysis section of this spec. 2. **Show the required column contract** the agent depends on for downstream logic: ``` Required columns in result rows: WorkLoadType, Environment, TestCaseName, IssueCategory, FrontLiners, Analysis, CanBeCaughtInInnerLoop Required placeholders in the .kql file: {{PIPELINE_TRIGGER_TIME}} (appears in main query AND join subquery) {{RESPONSIBLE_TEAM}} (replaced with kusto.bvt.queryVariables.RESPONSIBLE_TEAM at runtime) Tables referenced by default query: BvtDailyTestRunData (primary), BVTRawData (join — provides FrontLiners) ``` 3. **Ask the service-fit question** via `ask_user`: > *"The default query above is valid for services in **Azure Backup** (it queries `BvtDailyTestRunData` / `BVTRawData`). Does your service fall under Azure Backup?* > > *If your service is NOT an Azure Backup service, you'll likely need a different mechanism for BVT failure checking — I'll walk you through the options."* > Choices: `Yes — Azure Backup service`, `No — not an Azure Backup service` 4. **Branch on the answer**: **(A) `Yes — Azure Backup service`** (default path — MAB / DPM / Prot / BDP / similar): - Persist the default `.kql` file path to `kusto.bvt.queryFile` (e.g., `MAB-BVT-FailureAnalysis.kql`). If the file doesn't exist in `.github/skills/zed-agent/queries/`, copy the canonical version into it now. - **Do NOT prompt for `kusto.bvt.cluster` or `kusto.bvt.database`** — the default query targets a fixed Azure Backup cluster/database. Write these values directly: - `kusto.bvt.cluster` → `https://mabprod1.kusto.windows.net/` - `kusto.bvt.database` → `AzureBackup` - Ask only **one** field: - `kusto.bvt.queryVariables.RESPONSIBLE_TEAM` — value used by the agent to filter rows attributable to your team (e.g., `Prot`, `MABS`) - Note to release owner: *"Cluster `https://mabprod1.kusto.windows.net/` and database `AzureBackup` are fixed for the default Azure Backup BVT query. If results look wrong later, you can edit `.github/skills/zed-agent/queries/{queryFile}` directly — the agent re-reads it on every run."* **(B) `No — not an Azure Backup service`**: - First, show the release owner the available BVT failure-detection mechanisms supported by this agent today: > *"The agent currently supports the following mechanisms for BVT failure detection:* > * (1) **Custom Kusto query** — you provide a KQL query the agent runs on your team's Kusto cluster after canary BVTs complete; the result rows are treated as failures.* > > *More mechanisms may be added later."* > Choices: `1) Custom Kusto query` - On `Custom Kusto query`, walk the owner through a guided setup so the resulting query is solid and re-runnable by the agent. Persist each answer immediately: 1. Ask `kusto.bvt.cluster` — Kusto cluster URL where the BVT data lives. 2. Ask `kusto.bvt.database` — database name on that cluster. 3. Ask the owner how they want to provide the KQL, via `ask_user`: > *"How do you want to provide your team's BVT query?"* > Choices: `Paste KQL now`, `Point me at a .kql file in this repo` 4. **If `Paste KQL now`**: collect the KQL via `ask_user` (multi-line), write it to `.github/skills/zed-agent/queries/<service-name>-bvt.kql`, and persist that path to `kusto.bvt.queryFile`. 5. **If `Point me at a .kql file in this repo`**: ask for the relative path, validate the file exists, and persist it to `kusto.bvt.queryFile`. 6. **Make the query agent-runnable** — the agent must analyze the submitted KQL and intelligently fill in / negotiate the runtime parameters it needs: - **Timestamp window**: scan the query for any of `ago(...)`, `datetime(...)`, `between(...)`, `now()`, or a `TimeStamp >=` predicate. If none reference a pipeline-driven anchor, tell the owner the agent's BVT step needs the query to be scoped to "since canary deploy started" and offer to inject the placeholder `{{PIPELINE_TRIGGER_TIME}}` in the right spot. Confirm the exact column to filter on (default `TimeStamp`) via `ask_user`. - **Team / service filter (or whatever scoping the query uses)**: don't assume every custom query scopes results with a `ResponsibleTeam == "<team>"` predicate — some teams use a completely different mechanism (e.g., a tag column, a build-id join, a namespace prefix on `TestCaseName`, a pre-filtered function in their own database, or no per-team filter at all because the cluster only holds their data). Ask the owner via `ask_user` how their query already narrows results to their service's BVT runs, with choices roughly: `Uses a {{RESPONSIBLE_TEAM}}-style column filter`, `Uses a different mechanism — let me describe it`, `No scoping needed — query is already service-specific`. Then: - On `Uses a {{RESPONSIBLE_TEAM}}-style column filter`: ask for the column name (e.g., `ResponsibleTeam`, `ServiceName`, `Owner`) and the match value, offer to inject `{{RESPONSIBLE_TEAM}}`, and collect `kusto.bvt.queryVariables.RESPONSIBLE_TEAM`. - On `Uses a different mechanism`: collect a free-text description of the mechanism via `ask_user` (persist to `kusto.bvt.scopingNotes` as a comment for future maintainers), then ask which placeholders — if any — the agent needs to substitute at runtime and what values to bind. Persist each placeholder under `kusto.bvt.queryVariables.<NAME>`. If the mechanism needs nothing dynamic (a build id, a stamp list, etc. is hard-coded by the owner inside the .kql file), just record the note and move on — do NOT force a `{{RESPONSIBLE_TEAM}}` placeholder. - On `No scoping needed`: leave `kusto.bvt.queryVariables` untouched and record `kusto.bvt.scopingNotes = "Query is pre-scoped — no runtime filter needed"`. - In all branches: confirm the final shape with the owner (echo the relevant section of the .kql + the placeholder list) before persisting. - **Failure semantics**: confirm with the owner that "a returned row = a failure to surface to the release owner" (the agent does not interpret severity — it just routes whatever rows come back). If the query also returns passes, instruct the owner to add a `where Result == false` (or equivalent) filter. - **Required columns for routing**: ask which columns the owner wants displayed in the failure summary (TestCaseName, Environment, Owner, Analysis link, etc.). Persist the column list to `kusto.bvt.displayColumns` so Steps 6/8/11 can render a consistent table even with a non-MAB schema. - **Additional placeholders**: if the owner referenced any other `{{...}}` tokens, prompt for each one and persist under `kusto.bvt.queryVariables.<NAME>`. 7. **Dry-run check (optional but recommended)**: offer to execute the finalized query once via the Kusto MCP against the cluster/database the owner just provided, using a recent `{{PIPELINE_TRIGGER_TIME}}` (e.g., `ago(7d)`) to confirm it returns rows in the expected shape. On error, surface the Kusto error verbatim and let the owner edit the file and re-run the dry-run. 8. **Show this hard reminder** before finishing: > ⚠️ **Contract**: Steps 6, 8, and 11 will run this query verbatim against the cluster/database you just provided, substituting `{{PIPELINE_TRIGGER_TIME}}`, `{{RESPONSIBLE_TEAM}}`, and any other placeholders you declared. Every returned row will be reported as a BVT failure. Edit `.github/skills/zed-agent/queries/{queryFile}` any time — the agent re-reads it on every run; no agent code change needed. 5. After persistence, recap to the release owner what was saved (cluster, database, query file path, team filter value, display columns). > **Note**: Phase 4b runs **after Group 11** because its prompts depend on `canaryRouting.mode` from `pipeline-catalog.json`. Skip ahead to **Group 5a** next. **Group 5a — Notifications (Groups)** Ask for: - `notifications.groups.permanent` — Email addresses that receive important release notifications (array) - `notifications.groups.cc` — CC recipients (array) - `notifications.groups.releaseOwner` — Distribution list of people who *could* be release owners — e.g., your team's release-owner rotation distribution list like `mab-release-owners@microsoft.com` (array). This is **NOT** the current release owner's personal email — that's auto-detected from the signed-in user during `setup`. This distribution list receives release-owner-targeted notifications (R2D created, etc.) so the whole rotation has visibility. - `notifications.groups.teams` — Teams chat names for notifications (array) - `notifications.groups.teamsExtended` — Extended Teams chats for commit requests (array, can be subset of teams) **Group 5b — Notifications (Routing)** Routing is **per step, per outcome**. Each of the 16 pipeline steps has three outcomes: - **success** — step finished OK (also covers `skipped` and intermediate progress like EV2 stage ticks). - **failure** — step ended in failure. - **halt** — pipeline paused (unexpected halt OR waiting for an approval gate). The release owner is **always** added to every notification by `Resolve-NotificationRecipients.ps1` — there is no `includeOwner` field. Any step/outcome not listed in `notifications.routing` defaults to owner-only, so the JSON only needs entries that broadcast wider than the owner. Ensure the default routing block exists in `service-config.json` first — if `notifications.routing` is missing or empty, write the four seeded entries from the Generation section (`1-send-reminder.success`, `4-collect-commits.success`, `13-create-r2d.success`, `15-production-rollout.success`). Then read it back and **render the full 16-step table** to the release owner. Use `—` (em dash) for empty/owner-only cells. Each outcome cell shows `emailGroups` / `ccGroups` / `teamsGroups` separated by ` / `. Example of what the agent renders (with the owner's actual values, not these placeholders): | Step | success (email / cc / teams) | failure (email / cc / teams) | halt (email / cc / teams) | | ---- | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------- | | `1-send-reminder` | `permanent` / — / `teams` | — / — / — | — / — / — | | `2-cut-branch` | — / — / — | — / — / — | — / — / — | | `3-wait-build` | — / — / — | — / — / — | — / — / — | | `4-collect-commits` | — / — / `teamsExtended` | — / — / — | — / — / — | | `5-deploy-canary` | — / — / — | — / — / — | — / — / — | | `6-bvt-check` | — / — / — | — / — / — | — / — / — | | `7-rollback` | — / — / — | — / — / — | — / — / — | | `8-post-rollback-bvt` | — / — / — | — / — / — | — / — / — | | `9-post-rollback-signoff` | — / — / — | — / — / — | — / — / — | | `10-roll-forward` | — / — / — | — / — / — | — / — / — | | `11-post-rollforward-bvt` | — / — / — | — / — / — | — / — / — | | `12-post-rollforward-signoff` | — / — / — | — / — / — | — / — / — | | `13-create-r2d` | `releaseOwner` / `cc` / — | — / — / — | — / — / — | | `14-crb-review` | — / — / — | — / — / — | — / — / — | | `15-production-rollout` | `permanent`, `cc`, `releaseOwner` / — / — | — / — / — | — / — / — | | `16-merge-back` | — / — / — | — / — / — | — / — / — | After the table, add this one-line footnote: > *— means owner-only. The release owner is always on the To-line of every notification regardless of what's in the table. Cells override that default by adding distribution lists / Teams chats.* Then ask: > *"Edit routing?"* > Choices: `Keep as-is`, `Edit a cell`, `Done` Loop on the choice until the owner picks `Keep as-is` or `Done`: - **`Edit a cell`** — ask for the step (e.g., `6-bvt-check`), then the outcome (`success` / `failure` / `halt`), then which fields to change (`emailGroups`, `ccGroups`, `teamsGroups`). For each field, collect a comma-separated list of group keys from `notifications.groups` (Group 5a) and validate every entry against that list; re-ask on invalid input. To clear a cell back to owner-only, pass an empty list (the agent removes the field; if all three fields are empty it removes the outcome; if all three outcomes are empty it removes the step entry). Persist immediately and re-render the table. After the loop exits, run schema validation on the persisted routing block. If validation fails (e.g., owner referenced a group key not in Group 5a), surface the exact error and re-prompt for the offending cell only. > An owner can re-run just routing later with the shortcut `setup-service group 5b`. Re-running starts from the current table. **Group 6 — SafeFly / R2D** Ask for: - `safefly.titleTemplate` — R2D title template. Suggest: `[MAB][{serviceName}] {serviceDisplayName} monthly release for {month}-{yy}` - `safefly.tags` — SafeFly tags array (e.g., ["Prot_Regular_Rollout"]) - `safefly.additionalNotifiers` — Extra emails notified on SafeFly changes (array) - `safefly.genevaMdmLink` — Geneva MDM monitoring link **Group 7 — Commit Excel** Ask for: - `commitExcel.sheetNameTemplate` — Sheet name template (e.g., "Prot{{YYMM}}Commits"). `{{YYMM}}` is replaced at runtime. - `commitExcel.sharePointFolder` — SharePoint folder path (e.g., "/Shared Documents/Monthly Releases") **Group 8 — SharePoint** Ask for: - `sharepoint.sitePath` — SharePoint site path for Graph API auto-detection (e.g., "/teams/AzureBackupDataPlane", "/teams/MyTeamSite") Tell the release owner: *"This is the path portion of your team's SharePoint site URL. For example, if your SharePoint is at `microsoft.sharepoint.com/teams/MyTeam`, enter `/teams/MyTeam`."* **Group 9 — Operational Parameters** Show defaults and ask if the release owner wants to change any: - `operational.buildTimeoutMinutes` — default: 360 (6 hours) - `operational.bvtWaitHours` — default: 24 - `operational.canaryBakeTimeHours` — default: 24 - `operational.canaryRegions` — array of short region names (e.g., ["EACan", "ECY", "CCY"]) - `operational.watcherPollIntervalSeconds` — default: 3600 (1 hour) - `operational.watcherTaskPrefix` — default: "ZED-ReleaseWatcher" Tell the release owner: *"These defaults work well for most services. Only change if your service has specific timing requirements."* **Group 10 — Step Gates** Show all 16 steps with their default gate settings: ``` Step 1 send-reminder: OFF Step 2 cut-branch: OFF Step 3 wait-build: OFF Step 4 collect-commits: OFF Step 5 deploy-canary: OFF Step 6 bvt-check: ON ← release owner reviews BVT results Step 7 rollback: OFF Step 8 post-rollback-bvt: OFF Step 9 post-rollback-signoff: ON ← release owner approves post-rollback Step 10 roll-forward: OFF Step 11 post-rollforward-bvt: OFF Step 12 post-rollforward-signoff: ON ← release owner approves post-rollforward Step 13 create-r2d: OFF Step 14 crb-review: ON ← ALWAYS ON (non-overridable) Step 15 production-rollout: OFF Step 16 merge-back: OFF ``` Explain what a gate is, then ask whether to change defaults. Use this exact phrasing: > *"A **gate** is a pause point. When a step's gate is **ON**, the pipeline stops there and waits for you to type `approve-step <N>` (or `approve`) before moving to the next step. When **OFF**, that step auto-advances with no human input.* > > *Example: Step 6 (BVT Check) gate is ON by default — after canary BVTs run, the agent shows you the results and waits. You eyeball them, then type `approve-bvt` to continue to rollback. If you turned this gate OFF, the agent would auto-proceed to Step 7 the moment BVTs pass.* > > *The recommended defaults gate the 4 human-judgment steps (6 BVT review, 9 post-rollback sign-off, 12 post-roll-forward sign-off, 14 CRB review) and let the other 12 steps auto-flow. Step 14 is always ON and cannot be turned off — CRB approval is mandatory.* > > *Would you like to change any gates? You can also adjust them later any time with `gate on <N>` / `gate off <N>`."* **Group 11 — Pipeline Catalog** This generates `pipeline-catalog.json`. **Critical insight:** every service's pipelines have *different* `templateParameters` keys — there is **no fixed schema**. The agent treats `templateParameters` as a **free-form, pass-through key-value object**. Whatever the release owner provides is forwarded verbatim to the ADO pipeline trigger API at runtime. Do **not** assume a fixed set of keys; do **not** reject unknown keys.
